title: A calm guide to Ascend
sub: Six honest answers to the questions parents ask most. Every number below is read live from our rules.

faq.q: Will my child fall into debt?
faq.a: The limit is small: {limit_pct}% of what lands in their account each month, between {limit_min} and {limit_max}. The bill is paid in full every cycle, and if it isn't, spends pause straight away. There's no way to build up a big balance.

No. Interest if the bill is paid on time: {interest_pct}%. Processing fee: {processing_fee}. Annual fee: {annual_fee}. Late fee: {late_fee}. All of these are listed in the Key Fact Statement your child must read before agreeing.

faq.q: Will anyone call us or harass us if they're late?
faq.a: Never. Reminders go only to your child. After {grace_days} grace days spends pause, and if a bill stays unpaid we offer a {hardship_months}-month repayment plan. Any recovery is done only by {partner}, a regulated bank, under RBI rules. We never contact family, friends or college.

faq.q: Is this one of those shady loan apps?
faq.a: No. The money is lent by {partner}, which is regulated by the RBI; Ascend is the app that helps students use it well. We never ask for contacts, photos, SMS or location, and complaints go to a named grievance officer, with escalation to the RBI after {grievance_days} days.

faq.q: Why does a credit history matter at this age?
faq.a: Banks decide on future loans, rentals and even some jobs using credit history. Starting with a small limit and paying on time builds that history safely. A missed payment is reported to the bureaus only after {bureau_report_dpd} days, giving plenty of time to fix it.

faq.q: Can I see what my child spends?
faq.a: Only if they choose to share, and even then you see their on-time status, streak and progress, never what they bought or how much. They can switch the link off at any time. It's their record to build.

foot: Still unsure? Ask your child to show you the Key Fact Statement. Every fee is on it.
